title: Hygiene management in outpatient medical practices in the One Health Region Western Pomerania
summary:
Good hygiene in medical practices protects patients from infections and slows the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. 
So far, there are no regional data on this for general and specialist practices in Western Pomerania. 
In this study, practice owners and staff therefore complete an anonymous questionnaire, either on paper or online. Questions include whether the practice has a hygiene plan, how often staff are trained, how disinfectants are used and where respondents would like more training. 
The results will show where practices in the region are well prepared and where support could help.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Office-based general and specialist practices in the One Health Region Western Pomerania (districts of Vorpommern-Greifswald and Vorpommern-Ruegen) whose responsible person voluntarily agrees to take part. 
Group practices, joint practices and medical care centres (MVZ) count as one practice, practice-sharing arrangements as several. Sites at different addresses count separately. Staff survey: adult staff members of the participating practices.
Exclusion criteria:
Inpatient facilities, facilities without an independent outpatient practice structure and facilities outside the One Health Region Western Pomerania. 
Dental practices are excluded because separate doctoral projects on hygiene management in dental practices have already been carried out at the same institute. 
Staff under 18, for example trainees, are not surveyed.
